standard_prerequisites.name: A direct sum of modules each annihilated by a power of I is again I-power torsion, and a submodule and a quotient of an I-power torsion module are I-power torsion

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjection onto M with power torsion source whose kernel is power torsion produces the first two terms of the resolution, and the construction can be iterated
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the single surjection into the infinite resolution of the statement by repeating the construction on the kernel.

core_obligations: Display the canonical surjection from the direct sum over m in M of R over I^{n_m} onto M, where n_m is the smallest positive integer with I^{n_m} m = 0, and observe that it is onto because m itself is the image of the class of 1 in its own summand (proof lines 24014-24018).

Note that the source of this surjection is I-power torsion, being a direct sum of modules annihilated by powers of I, and that its kernel K_0 is a submodule of a power torsion module, hence also I-power torsion (proof lines 24018-24019).

Apply the same construction to the kernel K_0 and proceed inductively: each step produces a term K_i which is a direct sum of copies of R over I^n for varying n, and the next kernel to which the construction is applied (proof lines 24019-24020).
Conclude that M admits the resolution displayed in the statement, a long exact sequence with each K_i of the stated form, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 24013-24020).
proof_roadmap: Choose the exponent n_m attached to each element m of M and write down the canonical surjection from the direct sum of the quotients R over I^{n_m} onto M (proof lines 24014-24018).
Check that the source is power torsion and that the kernel is again power torsion, so the hypothesis of the lemma is inherited by the kernel (proof lines 24018-24019).
Repeat the construction on the successive kernels to obtain the resolution, every term of which is a direct sum of copies of R over powers of I (proof lines 24019-24020).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that every I-power torsion module M admits a resolution by direct sums of copies of R over I^n for varying n (statement lines 24001-24011). The proof is a compact but complete construction: it exhibits the canonical surjection from the direct sum over the elements m of M of the modules R over I^{n_m}, where n_m is the smallest exponent killing m, observes that the source is power torsion and that its kernel is a submodule of a power torsion module and therefore again power torsion, and iterates the same step on the successive kernels (proof lines 24014-24020). The two points that make the induction work are the choice of the exponent attached to each element and the inheritance of power torsionness by submodules, and both are stated explicitly.
